source.title: Number of Ways to Select Buildings

teaching.hint: For a fixed middle building, how many eligible choices can lie before and after it?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Every valid triple has a unique middle index, and its two outer types are the opposite of that middle type; left and right choices are independent.
solution_outline.approach: Count zeros and ones overall and while scanning. At each middle index, multiply the number of opposite-type positions before it by those after it, then sum.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The running prefix counts describe positions strictly before the current index; total counts minus the prefix and current position give the suffix counts.
solution_outline.correctness: Each valid triple contributes to exactly its own middle index and one independent left/right choice. The product counts every such choice once, so the sum is exact.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space; use wide arithmetic for up to roughly n³ triples.
solution_outline.pitfall: Reading “consecutive” as adjacent street positions excludes valid skipped-index choices.

common_wrong_turns: Require selected indices to be adjacent
source_fidelity_notes: Clarified selected-index consecutiveness and nonadjacent street positions without relying on boldface source markup.
